# Introduction

Testing cell proportional differences from single-cell-resolved count data became essential in modern tissue analyses. This task, becomes a repeated-measures question as soon as several observation from the same tissue donor. For example, we might profile multiple tumor cores, such as is common in tissue microarrays (TMA). Time course profiling or such as serial biopsies add a further level of complexity. Averaging cores up to the patient, then testing one phenotype at a time, drops both the compositional constraint and the repeated-measures structure.

[sccomp](https://github.com/MangiolaLaboratory/sccomp) is a flexible Bayesian model for mixed-effect designs, able to identify outliers probabilistically, test for differential variability and remove unwanted effects. sccomp accepts a long tibble, one row per sample and cell type, a count, and the design columns, and `sccomp_estimate()`, `sccomp_test()`, and `sccomp_predict()` return tibbles for `dplyr`, `tidyr`, and `ggplot2`. The [reproducible pipeline](#reproducible-sccomp-pipeline) below is that workflow.


# Source study and study design

We showcase [sccomp](https://github.com/MangiolaLaboratory/sccomp) capabilities on the NeoTrip trial. [Wang *et al.* (2023)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06498-3) used imaging mass cytometry (IMC) to map how multicellular spatial organization in triple-negative breast cancer relates to neoadjuvant immunotherapy response. The work is based on the NeoTRIP phase III trial (NCT02620280): early high-risk TNBC patients were randomised 1:1 to carboplatin + nab-paclitaxel (C) or the same regimen plus atezolizumab (C&I), with eight 3-week neoadjuvant cycles before surgery. Research FFPE biopsies:

- Baseline (*n* = 243)
- On-treatment (first day of cycle 2; *n* = 207)
- Post-treatment (surgical excision; *n* = 210)
- Profiled with a 43-marker IMC panel at subcellular resolution
- Deep-learning segmentation and semi-supervised clustering defined 17 epithelial and 20 TME cell phenotypes
- Multiple regions of interest (ROIs) were imaged per biopsy

Each patient contributes several samples. The biopsies are nested in the patient, and the regions of interest are nested in the biopsy. Patient NT193, in the chemotherapy arm with residual disease, was imaged at all three timepoints: 10 ROIs at baseline, 10 on-treatment, and 3 at surgery. In the model, each ROI is one compositional sample and the patient is the repeated-measures group.

# sccomp mixed-effects compositional modelling

**In the original publication**, longitudinal composition was summarised as mean phenotype proportions per patient and compared across arms, timepoints, and response groups using Wilcoxon tests and *Z*-scored trend plots (Fig. 5). Phenotypes were also tested individually with weighted binomial GLMs on tumour-level proportions. These approaches treat each phenotype separately, aggregate ROIs to the patient before inference, and do not jointly model compositional closure (proportions within a compartment sum to one) or hierarchical repeated measures (multiple biopsies and ROIs nested within the same patient).

**Here** we reproduce and extend that compositional dynamics analysis using [sccomp](https://github.com/MangiolaLaboratory/sccomp). sccomp, directly modelling count data, parameterises composition on a latent log-ratio scale and fits mixed effects on the mean and variability structure. Each ROI (`ImageID`) is one compositional sample; a patient random intercept `(1 | PatientID)` absorbs baseline and trajectory differences across individuals and shrinkage across the cohort. 

$$\text{composition} \sim \text{Arm} \times \text{BiopsyPhase} \times \text{pCR} + (1 \mid \text{PatientID})$$


# sccomp analysis

The blocks below are the minimal tidyverse code to reproduce the analysis locally from the parsed input (run top to bottom), using the immune TME compartment with ROI-level samples and a patient random intercept. 

## From long-format tidy input

The input `long` is a tibble with one row per ROI × immune phenotype: a count plus the design columns (`Arm`, `BiopsyPhase`, `pCR`) and the grouping `PatientID`. Preview:

## Fit the model


::: {.cell layout-align="center" cache.extra='2.5.1'}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="show" code-summary="Fit and test the model"}
library(sccomp)

fit <- sccomp_estimate(
  long,
  formula_composition = ~ Arm * BiopsyPhase * pCR + (1 | PatientID),
  formula_variability = ~ 1,
  sample = "sample",
  cell_group = "cell_group",
  abundance = "count",
  inference_method = "hmc",
  cores = parallel::detectCores(),
  verbose = FALSE
) |>
  sccomp_test()
```

## Hypothesis testing

We pass contrasts to `sccomp_test()` as strings. 

`marginal_CI_post` compares responders with residual disease at that visit alone. Any gap the two groups already had at baseline is still in this result.

`did_CI_post` compares how far each group moved from its own baseline. A head start cancels, so the result is the difference in change.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="show" code-summary="Test two contrasts"}
# The strings are the rows of the same design matrix sccomp fits.
grid <- expand.grid(
  Arm = factor(c("C", "C&I"), c("C", "C&I")),
  BiopsyPhase = factor(
    c("Baseline", "On-treatment", "Post-treatment"),
    c("Baseline", "On-treatment", "Post-treatment")
  ),
  pCR = factor(c("RD", "pCR"), c("RD", "pCR"))
)
mm <- model.matrix(~ Arm * BiopsyPhase * pCR, grid)
row_of <- function(a, p, r) mm[grid$Arm == a & grid$BiopsyPhase == p & grid$pCR == r, ]
to_expr <- function(v) {
  v <- v[abs(v) > 1e-9]
  paste(sprintf("%g * `%s`", v, names(v)), collapse = " + ")
}

contrasts <- c(
  marginal_CI_post = to_expr(
    row_of("C&I", "Post-treatment", "pCR") - row_of("C&I", "Post-treatment", "RD")
  ),
  did_CI_post = to_expr(
    (row_of("C&I", "Post-treatment", "pCR") - row_of("C&I", "Baseline", "pCR")) -
      (row_of("C&I", "Post-treatment", "RD") - row_of("C&I", "Baseline", "RD"))
  )
)

res <- sccomp_test(fit, contrasts = contrasts)
```

# Results

## Predicted immune compositional trajectories

**Figure 1** shows baseline-aligned predicted proportions (95% credible intervals) for all 15 immune TME phenotypes. Within each arm × cell-type facet, both response groups are shifted to the mean of their baseline predictions. Panels are split by treatment arm (columns); colour denotes pathological response. Asterisks mark arm–time points with difference-in-differences FDR \< 0.05.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="true" code-summary="Align groups to a common baseline"}
# Shift pCR and RD to their average baseline within each Arm x cell_group, per draw
shifts <- draws |>
  filter(BiopsyPhase == "Baseline") |>
  select(Arm, cell_group, .draw, pCR, proportion) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = pCR, values_from = proportion) |>
  mutate(shift_pCR = (pCR + RD) / 2 - pCR,
         shift_RD  = (pCR + RD) / 2 - RD) |>
  select(Arm, cell_group, .draw, shift_pCR, shift_RD)

aligned_summary <- draws |>
  left_join(shifts, by = c("Arm", "cell_group", ".draw")) |>
  mutate(aligned_prop = proportion + if_else(pCR == "pCR", shift_pCR, shift_RD)) |>
  summarise(
    aligned_mean  = mean(aligned_prop),
    aligned_lower = quantile(aligned_prop, 0.025),
    aligned_upper = quantile(aligned_prop, 0.975),
    .by = c(Arm, BiopsyPhase, pCR, cell_group)
  )
```

## Change from baseline

For each cell type and treatment arm, the hypothesis is that responders and patients with residual disease changed by a different amount from baseline. **Figure 2** shows that difference at two time points: the on-treatment and post-treatment. Bordered tiles have FDR \< 0.05.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code  code-summary="Difference-in-differences heatmap"}

did_hm[, cell_group := factor(cell_group, levels = rev(cell_order))]
did_hm <- did_hm[!is.na(cell_group)]
did_hm[, BiopsyPhase := factor(BiopsyPhase, levels = c("On-treatment", "Post-treatment"))]
did_hm[, Arm := factor(Arm, levels = c("C", "C&I"))]
did_hm[, sig := is.finite(c_FDR) & c_FDR < 0.05]
did_hm[, facet_lab := paste0(Arm, " · ", BiopsyPhase)]
did_hm[, facet_lab := factor(facet_lab, levels = c(
  "C · On-treatment", "C · Post-treatment",
  "C&I · On-treatment", "C&I · Post-treatment"

lim <- max(abs(did_hm$c_effect), na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(did_hm, aes(x = facet_lab, y = cell_group, fill = c_effect)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_tile(
    data = did_hm[sig == TRUE],

  geom_text(
```
